doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: His regular band and winging the set
summary: Person says he keeps a regular band, uses a circle of players in the studio, and does not write set lists.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Now I know musicians around here, including myself, have in our book, we have a list. If a gig comes up you say now who can I get on drums, and you go down and make your first choice. Is it the same for you? Do you have a circle of people that you call on or do you have the same people all the time?

Well in the recording studio I have a circle of people, because you have artists considerations too, the artists that you’re producing. But I have a regular band, same guys, the piano player’s been with us about ten years, ten or twelve years. So no, the same guys, yeah.
That’s great. There’s a lot to be said for having some arrangements worked out and having a sound.
Yeah we’ve got a sound. All by trial and error. Yeah I like to wing it. We wing it.
Do you write out a set before you go up on stage?
Yeah. I couldn’t follow it anyways. No it just rolls out, whatever it is.
